//: Hand-written skill descriptions. sync-skills.mjs PREFERS these over auto-extraction. Add an entry whenever the auto-extracted description reads badly - description quality is the whole routing mechanism in Claude Code. Keys must match a directory under .cursor/skills/.
api-consistency-audit: Audits an already-shipped .NET API surface for cross-endpoint consistency - route naming, versioning, DTO shape, pagination, error/ProblemDetails format, auth attribute placement and OpenAPI annotations across endpoints written at different times by different people. Use when asked whether the API is consistent, or to review the whole API surface rather than one endpoint.
architecture-map-gen: Generates live architecture diagrams from the real codebase: dependency-graph, ERD, service-map, service-interaction, data-flow, C4 and sequence diagrams, labelled with this team's own layer names from memory-bank/architecture.md. Use when asked to visualise, diagram or map the architecture, or to find dependency cycles.
enterprise-report-gen: Assembles a standardized executive-facing report by aggregating existing audit skills' output into one consistent template. Report types: architecture, security, performance, database, repository-health, technical-debt, production-readiness, release-readiness, dependency-health, code-quality. Use when asked for a readiness, health or status report for management.
pattern-finder: Finds the actual file in this repo that is the best existing example of what is about to be built, so generated code imitates real local convention instead of generic boilerplate. Runs silently as Step 0 of every *-gen skill. Use before generating any handler, endpoint, component, hook or repository. In Claude Code prefer the pattern-scout subagent, which does the same work in an isolated context.
platform-health-validator: Workspace-hygiene check over the whole cursor-platform install: verifies rules, skills, docs and memory-bank are internally consistent, cross-references resolve, and nothing has drifted out of sync. Use when asked whether the platform itself is healthy or correctly wired.
prompt-quality-audit: Scores a user prompt or spec for ambiguity, missing acceptance criteria, unstated constraints and hidden assumptions, then returns a rewritten version plus the clarifying questions worth asking. Use when a request is vague, or when asked to review or improve a prompt or spec before implementation.
skill-maturity-audit: Audits the skill library itself against the shared execution pipeline contract - checks each .cursor/skills/*/skill.md for correct dependency wiring, pattern-finder usage, memory references, output paths and category. Use when asked to verify skills are wired correctly, or after adding or editing a skill.
work-breakdown: Decomposes any unit of work - a spec, a traced feature, an impact-analysis result, a bug, a refactor, or a migration - into a validated board of tasks small enough for one agent session to finish. Presents vertical / horizontal / risk-first slicing options with tradeoffs, then enforces sizing with task-graph.mjs: max 8 files, max 2 layers, a verify command per task, no dependency cycles. Use when asked to break down, split, decompose, plan out, or sequence work, or when a task is too big to execute.
operability-gen: Generates the three artifacts that decide whether a feature can be RUN rather than merely built: SLI/SLO definitions with an error-budget policy, alert rules that link to a runbook, and the runbook itself. Alerts on symptoms not causes. Use when asked about SLOs, SLIs, error budgets, alerting, on-call, runbooks, monitoring thresholds, or what to do when a service breaks.
production-readiness-review: The Go/No-Go gate before a feature reaches production. Reviews seven dimensions - reliability and resilience, observability, deployability and reversibility, security and access, scalability and capacity, incident response, data and backups - and returns a blocking verdict with evidence. Use when asked whether something is ready to ship, ready for production, or safe to release.
delivery-metrics: Measures whether the platform is improving delivery or just producing code faster. Computes DORA four keys plus rework rate, change size and churn hotspots from git history via delivery-metrics.mjs, labelling each metric MEASURED or PROXY. Use when asked about deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, DORA, engineering productivity, or whether delivery is getting better or worse.
release-safety: Plans how a change reaches users without a big-bang cutover, and how it gets pulled back. Covers feature-flag lifecycle with mandatory owner and expiry, progressive rollout rings with gate metrics defined up front, an explicit rollback plan including what rollback does NOT undo, and expand-migrate-contract schema reversibility. Backed by flag-debt.mjs. Use when asked about rollout, canary, feature flags, rollback, deployment strategy, or migration safety.
threat-model: Applies STRIDE threat modelling at design time, before the code exists and while a fix is still a design change. Maps trust boundaries, walks spoofing/tampering/repudiation/information-disclosure/denial-of-service/elevation-of-privilege per element, hunts IDOR and business-logic abuse specifically, and assigns mitigate/transfer/accept/eliminate per threat. Use when asked to threat model, review a design for security, or assess attack surface before building.
postmortem: Runs a blameless incident review and converts each finding into the highest mechanical enforcement available - a BannedSymbols entry, an analyzer severity, an architecture test, a lint rule, or a hook tripwire - rather than a document nobody reads. Builds the timeline from git and calls out the impact-to-detected and detected-to-diagnosed gaps. Use after an incident, outage, production bug, or regression.
task-verify: Decides whether a task is actually done, from evidence, and blocks Done otherwise. Runs the task's Verify command and records the result, checks acceptance-criteria coverage via ac-trace.mjs, reads the tests for the failure modes a tool cannot catch (asserting the implementation, testing the mock, encoding the same misunderstanding as the code), and optionally runs mutation testing scoped to changed files. Use when asked to verify, validate, check, or sign off a task or feature, or whether something is really finished.
load-test-gen: Generates a runnable load test for a real user journey with thresholds taken from the SLOs already committed to. k6 or NBomber, profiles for smoke, load, stress, soak and spike. Covers the gap between dotnet-perf-profile (micro-benchmarks, in-process) and production-readiness-review (which blocks on a missing load test). Use when asked about load testing, stress testing, soak testing, throughput under concurrency, capacity, or how many users the system holds.
